passage:
Good morning, everyone, and welcome to Thornbury Wildlife Park. My name's Rosa, and I'm one of the rangers here. Before you set off, I'd like to give you a few pieces of information to help you enjoy your visit.

First, a word about the park itself. Many people think we're a zoo, but we're actually a conservation centre. Most of our animals came here because they were injured or couldn't survive in the wild, and our main aim is to breed rare native species and return them to nature. Last year, for example, we released forty water voles into local rivers.

Now, the most popular area is the otter enclosure. Feeding time used to be at eleven, but we've moved it to half past two, because the otters are much more active in the afternoon. So if you want to see them at their best, come back after lunch.

You'll notice there's a new walkway through the woodland. It was built last spring, and it goes right up into the trees, about eight metres above the ground. It's perfectly safe, but please note that it's closed in strong winds. Today the forecast is calm, so it should be open all day.

As for food, the main café is next to the gift shop. There's also a picnic area by the lake, but please don't feed the ducks bread. It's bad for them. You can buy special duck food at the café for fifty pence a bag.

Finally, we're running a photography competition this month. Upload your best animal photo to our website before the 30th. The prize is a family season ticket, and the winning picture will be printed in our guidebook next year.

Enjoy your day!

[Notes]
Picnic area: by the (4) ______ (do not feed ducks bread)
Photo competition prize: a family (5) ______ ticket
question: What is the main aim of the park?
choices: to return rare native animals to the wild
to display animals from around the world
to train people to work with animals
answer: to return rare native animals to the wild
explanation: 動物園と思われがちだが、主な目的は希少な在来種を繁殖させて自然に戻すことだと言っている。

Hello and thanks for tuning in to Community Radio's weekend guide. Today I'm going to tell you about the changes at Marsh End Wildlife Park, which reopens next Saturday after six months of work.

The biggest change is the new entrance. Previously, visitors arrived through the car park, which meant a long walk past the service buildings. Now the entrance is on the river side, and you can actually arrive by boat from the town centre. The boat runs every forty-five minutes, and although it's slower than driving, it's a lovely way to start the day.

Ticket prices have gone up slightly. An adult ticket is now fourteen pounds, rather than twelve. However, the park has introduced a new policy: if you visit on a weekday and show a library card from the local area, you get in for half price. The park's director told me this was to encourage local families who might not otherwise come.

Inside, there are some new residents. The park has two red pandas, which arrived from a breeding programme in the Netherlands. They're quite shy, so the keepers have asked visitors to stay quiet near their enclosure. Don't expect to see them straight away; they often sleep high in the trees until mid-morning.

The old reptile house has been completely rebuilt, and it's now a tropical butterfly house. It's kept at twenty-eight degrees, so you might want to take your coat off before you go in.

For children, there's a new activity trail with twelve wooden posts. At each post there's a question about the animals, and children who complete the trail can collect a badge from the information desk.

And finally, the park is looking for volunteers to help with guided walks. No experience is needed, but you must be available at least two weekends a month.

[Notes]
Former reptile house is now a tropical (4) ______ house
Children who finish the activity trail receive a (5) ______
question: What is new about the way visitors can arrive at the park?
choices: They can travel there by boat.
They can park closer to the entrance.
They can take a free bus from the town.
answer: They can travel there by boat.
explanation: 入口が川側に移り、町の中心からボートで来られるようになった。

Hi everyone. I'm Declan, and I'm the education officer here at Glenmoor Wildlife Park. Thanks for choosing us for your school trip. I'll explain how the day will work.

You'll be divided into three groups, and each group will spend about an hour in three different areas. We'd planned to begin with the farm area, but because the sheep are being sheared this morning, we'll start in the bird of prey centre instead, and visit the farm after lunch.

At the bird of prey centre, you'll meet our owls and eagles. You may be lucky enough to hold one of the smaller owls, but you'll have to wear a special leather glove. Their claws are very sharp. Please don't make sudden movements or loud noises, because the birds can get frightened.

Next is the pond. Here, you'll be using nets to catch small creatures like water beetles and snails. You will then look at them through a magnifying glass and record what you find on your worksheet. Remember to put everything back in the water afterwards.

Lunch will be in the education barn. If it's raining, you can eat inside, but on a dry day like today we'll use the tables outside. Please put all your rubbish in the recycling bins, which are green, not the general waste bins.

There is a gift shop, but teachers have asked that students don't visit it today, as time is limited.

Before you leave, every student will receive a pack of wildflower seeds to plant at school. They attract bees and butterflies. And if your class sends us photos of the flowers when they grow, we'll put them on our website.

Right, let's get going. Group one, follow me.

[Notes]
At the pond: look at creatures through a magnifying (4) ______
Each student receives: a pack of wildflower (5) ______
question: Why will the groups start at the bird of prey centre?
choices: The sheep are being sheared in the morning.
The birds are only active in the morning.
The farm area is closed for repairs.
answer: The sheep are being sheared in the morning.
explanation: 羊の毛刈りが午前中にあるので、農場ではなく猛禽類センターから始める。

passage:
Good evening, and thank you all for coming to this information session about the reopening of Fernley Town Hall. I'm Joanna Pike from the council's events team.

As you know, the building was closed for nearly two years while it was renovated. The original plan was to finish last autumn, but when the builders removed the old ceiling, they discovered some beautiful painted panels from the nineteenth century, and these had to be carefully restored. That's why the opening was delayed until this month.

So, what's changed? The main hall now has a new sound system and seating for 450 people, which is a hundred more than before. The seats can also be removed, so the hall can be used for dances and markets as well as concerts.

On the ground floor, the old council offices have been turned into a public café. It will be run by a local charity that trains young people for jobs in catering. It'll be open from nine until five, every day except Monday.

Many of you asked about access. There's now a lift to every floor, and the main entrance has a ramp. However, the side entrance on Church Street is still only reachable by steps, so we recommend wheelchair users use the front.

The clock tower has also been repaired. For the first time in thirty years, the bells will ring every hour, although they'll be silent at night between 11 p.m. and 7 a.m.

Finally, the opening celebration will be on Saturday the 22nd. There'll be music, food stalls and free tours of the building every half an hour. The tours are free, but you need to book a place on the council website, because numbers are limited to twenty per tour.

[Notes]
Clock tower bells: silent from 11 p.m. to (4) ______ a.m.
Building tours: free but must (5) ______ online
question: Why was the reopening of the town hall delayed?
choices: Old painted panels were found and needed restoring.
The builders found problems with the roof.
The council ran out of money.
answer: Old painted panels were found and needed restoring.
explanation: 古い天井を外したら19世紀の絵が描かれたパネルが見つかり、修復が必要になったため。

Welcome to the newly renovated Ashby Town Hall. I'm Martin, one of the volunteer guides, and over the next forty minutes I'll take you round the building.

We're standing in the entrance hall, which is the oldest part, built in 1782. During the renovation, the architects wanted to keep as much of the original structure as possible, but they also needed to make the building far more energy-efficient. The solution they chose was quite clever. Rather than replacing the old windows, which are protected, they fitted a second layer of glass on the inside. You can hardly see it, but it has cut heating costs by around a third.

If you look down, you'll see the floor is made of local stone. Some visitors assume it's new, but in fact it's the original floor. It was hidden under carpet for decades, and it only had to be cleaned.

Now, follow me into the council chamber. This used to be where local politicians met, and it still is, once a month. But on other days it's available for hire. It's become very popular for weddings, which has been a useful source of income for the town.

Upstairs, there's a new local history gallery. The displays were put together with help from residents, who lent old photographs and objects. The most popular item is a fire engine bell from 1890, which you're allowed to ring, gently.

At the very top is the roof terrace. It wasn't part of the original plan, but when the builders replaced the roof, they realised there was space for one. It's open to the public on summer evenings and gives wonderful views of the river.

Before we go up, a reminder that the gallery shop sells postcards and books about the town, and all profits go towards maintaining the building.

[Notes]
Most popular gallery item: a fire engine (4) ______ from 1890
Roof terrace: open on summer (5) ______
question: How was the building made more energy-efficient?
choices: Extra glass was added inside the old windows.
The old windows were replaced with modern ones.
Solar panels were put on the roof.
answer: Extra glass was added inside the old windows.
explanation: 保護された古い窓は替えずに、内側にもう一層ガラスを付けた。

Hello, this is a recorded message from Bramwell Town Hall. Thank you for calling. The town hall reopened to the public in March after renovation, and this message gives information about our services and events.

Our opening hours have changed. The building is now open from 8.30 a.m. to six p.m. on weekdays. On Saturdays it opens from ten until four, and it's closed on Sundays, except when there's a special event.

The library has moved from Market Street into the town hall, and it's now on the first floor. It's larger than before, with a separate room for children. Please note that the library's computers can now only be used if you book in advance, because they've become so popular.

The main hall is available to hire for private parties, meetings and classes. The price is twenty-five pounds an hour for local residents, or forty pounds for non-residents. There's a discount for registered charities. For more information, please email the bookings office rather than calling, as the office is only staffed in the mornings.

This month's events include a classical concert on Friday the 8th, performed by the town orchestra. Tickets cost eight pounds, and children under twelve go free. On the 15th, there's a talk about the history of the building by a local historian, who'll show photographs of the hall from the 1920s.

We also run a weekly coffee morning every Wednesday for people over sixty. It's a chance to meet new people, and there's no need to book.

Parking: the town hall car park now has spaces for electric vehicles, but the car park is small, so we encourage visitors to use public transport. The number 4 bus stops right outside.

Thank you for calling.

[Notes]
Library now on: (4) ______ floor
Number of the bus that stops outside: (5) ______

choices: They must be booked in advance.
They are only available to children.
They can be used free of charge.
answer: They must be booked in advance.
explanation: 人気が高くなったので、事前予約しないと使えない。

Hi everyone, and thanks for signing up for the Coastline Cycle Challenge. I'm Neha, the event organiser, and I'll run through the important points before Sunday.

There are three routes this year. The family route is fifteen kilometres and completely flat, along the old railway path. The middle route is forty kilometres, and the long route is a hundred. Last year the long route started in the town square, but because of roadworks, it will start from the sports centre instead. All the other routes still start in the square.

Registration opens at 7.30 on the day. When you arrive, you'll get a number to attach to the front of your bike, and a wristband. Please don't lose the wristband, because you'll need it to collect your medal and free meal at the end.

There'll be three food stations along the long route and one on the middle route. They'll offer water, fruit and energy bars. We've decided not to give out plastic bottles this year, to reduce waste, so please bring your own bottle, and you can refill it at every station.

Safety is important. Helmets are compulsory, and anyone without one won't be allowed to start. There'll be first aid volunteers on motorbikes along all the routes, and if you have a mechanical problem, call the number printed on the back of your rider number.

This year, the event is raising money for the children's ward at the local hospital. So far, we've raised just over eight thousand pounds, and our target is ten thousand. If you haven't already, please ask friends and family to sponsor you.

Finally, the weather forecast is good, but it could be windy on the coast road, so bring an extra layer.

[Notes]
Wristband needed to collect: medal and free (4) ______
Money raised for: the hospital's children's (5) ______

choices: the sports centre
the town square
the old railway path
explanation: 道路工事のため、長距離ルートは広場ではなくスポーツセンターから出発する。

Good afternoon. I'm Callum Reid from the city council's transport department, and I'm here to talk about Car-Free Day, which takes place on the first Sunday of June.

On that day, eight kilometres of city centre streets will be closed to motor traffic from nine in the morning until four in the afternoon, and opened up to cyclists, walkers and skaters. This is the third year we've held the event. The first year, we closed only the riverside road, and it was so crowded that some people complained they couldn't actually ride. So last year we expanded the area, and this year we're adding the route round the park as well.

A question we often get is whether people need to register. You don't, unless you're joining the guided rides. These are led by experienced cyclists and are designed for people who haven't cycled in the city before. They leave every hour from the cathedral, and places are limited, so do sign up online.

For those without a bike, the city's bike-share scheme will be free all day. Normally you'd pay a pound for every thirty minutes. There will also be a free repair station outside the central library, where mechanics will check brakes and tyres.

We've listened to feedback from local businesses. In the past, some shop owners worried that closing roads would reduce their customers. In fact, our surveys showed that most shops on the route did more business than on a normal Sunday, particularly cafés. This year, we're inviting businesses to put tables on the street.

One more thing: buses will be diverted, not cancelled, so check the transport website for details. And there's a family picnic in the park at one o'clock, with live music.

[Notes]
Free bike repair station: outside the central (4) ______
Family picnic with live music: in the (5) ______ at 1 p.m.
question: Why was the car-free area made larger after the first year?
choices: It was too crowded to cycle comfortably.
Local shops asked for more streets to be closed.
The riverside road was being repaired.
answer: It was too crowded to cycle comfortably.
explanation: 初年度は混みすぎて走れないという苦情があったので範囲を広げた。
